newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close lower on election blues.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close lower on election blues.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks ended slightly lower on Tuesday after moving in a tight range as investors stayed on the sidelines anticipating more violence ahead of March local government polls, brokers said.
The all-share index closed 1.03 points down at 614.37. Price declines outnumbered gains by 23 to eight, but rises in blue chips Hayleys Ltd and Richard Pieris & Co supported the index.
"Buyers are waiting to see if there will be any more violence before the election," said Thikshan Arulampalem, a trader at Lanka Securities.
A ruling party lawmaker was gunned down last week, a day before nominations closed for the March 21 polling, raising the possibility of more violence in the run-up to elections.

"We have had some inquiries from new overseas investors, but as to if and when these will materialise into firm orders will be seen only after the election," said Rohan Fernando, a broker at CT Smith stock brokerage.
Turnover, helped by foreign buying of 15,600 Lion Brewery shares and 4,300 of Hayleys, was 9.4 million rupees.
Foreign buying amounted to 2.9 million rupees, and selling was 532,459 rupees. -- Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
